correctness.rationale: For commuting Pauli strings the number of common sites with different axes is even. A conflict at v therefore forces a common second site w and identical two-site support. Any term touching just one of v,w would have to use an axis commuting with two different axes, which is impossible. On the pair, the two independent commuting generators have exactly their four-element Pauli span as centralizer modulo phases. Local Clifford rotations make it the Bell Pauli span and preserve the individual collected coefficient bounds; all other sites are single-axis and locally diagonal. The Gibbs state factors over the isolated pairs and the diagonal part. Partial transposition of each Bell projector gives half the identity minus a projector onto a permuted Bell vector (by transposing the maximally entangled projector and conjugating by local Paulis); the mixture has spectrum {1/2−q_s}. Two-qubit PPT is sufficient, and tracing to each pair gives the converse for full separability. Trace norms multiply, with factors of 1 from the diagonal Gibbs sector and all noncrossing pairs, and max(1,2p_e) from crossing pairs. Any two Bell sign triples differ in exactly two coordinates, so the maximum energy gap is 4J. The largest weight is consequently at most (1+3exp(−4βJ))^−1. The degree-two Hamiltonian J(XX+YY+ZZ) gives one energy −3J and three at +J, attains that bound, and is NPT exactly above βJ=ln(3)/4. This proves sufficiency and necessity, including the endpoint, for every cap Δ≥2.
residual_risks: The stored subset enumerations and floating-point PT comparisons are finite corroboration, not independent replay or certificates of the general result. The coefficient bound applies after collecting duplicate strings, and the finite-dimensional zero-temperature statement is understood as a limit.

evidence: Commuting interaction algebras give preserved sectors and disjoint-edge factors within sectors. Bell-diagonal PPT gives the dimer law without a new entanglement criterion. The examined Bouland et al. result is for a fixed commuting two-qubit interaction and uses arbitrary basis change.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The Pauli property is used to obtain globally fixed isolated pairs, not merely sectorwise weak entanglement of eigenvectors. Arbitrary unitary changes need not preserve a per-Pauli coefficient bound. With the fixed partition in place, the all-cut identity is a direct tensor-product consequence, not an independent new dimer formula.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A matching of the term-overlap graph is a different restriction from the matching of isolated site pairs here. The three-term dimer has a term-overlap triangle and is not included by either criterion.

originality.rationale: The standard Bell-pair PPT law and the isotropic dimer crossing temperature are not themselves new. The supported contribution is the coefficient-preserving fixed-matching reduction for this Pauli class and the exact global consequences proved from it, particularly uniform optimality of the Heisenberg witness over arbitrary systems. Neither the closest unrestricted-locality result nor the inspected structural or degree-one results give those consequences under the stated hypotheses.
residual_risks: An implicit restricted-locality thermal corollary elsewhere remains possible. The bounded retrieval did not yield full text for DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.017901 or DOI 10.1103/PhysRevA.54.1838; the familiar single-dimer calculations are not part of the priority claim.

value.rationale: For a physically natural restricted class the result isolates all finite-temperature quantum correlations into pairs even when the classical interaction graph is complex. It gives an exact separability decision and cut-by-cut quantitative entanglement without many-body Gibbs diagonalization, and a strictly improved, attained universal temperature boundary compared with the unrestricted-locality degree-two bound.
residual_risks: No claim for higher-weight terms, qudits, noncommuting models, or distillability; the value is in exact control of this class rather than a new general thermal bound.
